A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Di4C research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 distillation results and ablations, including FID and inception scores in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and reports original ImageNet and language-generation experiments, latency measurements and additional analyses.

M1.justification: The core mixture model and distillation/consistency losses remain. v2 extends training to mixture teachers for repeated Di4C rounds (A.4), introduces transformer conditioning through an additional lambda token, and selects between the existing losses according to time in the masked-model implementations (F.3.4 and F.4.2).

E1.justification: Beyond the retained CIFAR-10 pixel-generation task, v2 adds ImageNet 256×256 class-conditional generation in a quantized representation, OpenWebText language modeling and unconditional generation, and WebText-prompted continuations. These substantially broaden the domains, representations and task requirements.

E2.justification: The CIFAR-10 analytical-sampling and tau-leaping comparators remain in v2 Table 3. New comparisons evaluate the Besnier–Chen MaskGIT teacher and SDTT round-6 and round-7 checkpoints against Di4C variants (Figures 3–4), substantially extending the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The original CIFAR-10 protocol is retained. New protocols include ImageNet guidance sweeps and test-reference FID/IS using 50,000 class-balanced samples; language evaluation adds GPT-2-large perplexity, Self-BLEU and MAUVE, with specified generation lengths and prompt counts. The added experiments also introduce distinct training budgets, sampling schedules and latency-testing procedures.

E4.justification: The original control-variate, loss-weight and lambda-sample-size ablations survive as v2 Tables 4–5. v2 adds comparisons testing auxiliary data loss and repeated distillation, measurements of mixture-model latency overhead, and qualitative image and text comparisons (F.1, F.3 and F.4). These address several previously untested questions.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2 newly reports average latency and standard deviation over 10 batches, with batch sizes specified in F.1. The original CIFAR-10 inception-score uncertainty is preserved in Tables 3–5. No increase in training-run or seed counts is reported.

E6.justification: The original CIFAR-10 numerical results are retained. Substantial new results include ImageNet FID 6.57 for four-step di4c-d and eight-step teacher sampling at separately selected guidance coefficients (Table 6), language perplexity/diversity and MAUVE curves, and measured runtime overhead (Table 2). These are added results under new settings, rather than revised CIFAR-10 performance.

T1.justification: v2 removes the full-support assumption required by v1's Theorem 3 upper bound. Proposition 5 is restricted to positive-probability conditioning states, and Lemma 1 changes from a uniform C epsilon² bound to C epsilon²/q_t(x), with a substantially revised proof in D.4. This materially broadens the stated guarantee, although the revised lemma has an internal counterexample described in the overall assessment.

C1.justification: The mixture-model and distillation contributions remain, but the abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the empirical claims substantially. v1 claims improvements in few-step CIFAR-10 sampling; v2 additionally claims approximately twofold ImageNet acceleration and further distillation of already-distilled language models while preserving diversity.

C2.justification: v2 removes the broad VLB-based loss criticism and focuses Section 2.2 on limitations of learning continuous-time transition rates. It adds an explanation of ImageNet timing through sampling bottlenecks and qualifications about cross-paper Self-BLEU comparisons. The original CIFAR-10 correlation hypothesis survives in F.2.2, and the gap between theoretical one-step distillation and practical acceleration remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 adds extensive transformer architecture, lambda-embedding, optimizer, batch-size, hardware and training-budget information for the new experiments. It also supplies SDTT checkpoint-loading instructions and evaluation-code references, including detailed Self-BLEU tokenization, weighting and smoothing settings. The original CIFAR-10 implementation recipe is largely retained.

R1.justification: The new related-work section substantially expands positioning around MaskGIT, MDLM, SDTT and energy-based diffusion language models. It explains compatibility with existing acceleration methods and contrasts mixture sampling with approaches requiring additional models or importance sampling. This goes beyond the change from numbered to author–year citations.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and dimensional-correlation discussion, reverses the mixture-model and loss-function subsections, and introduces a dedicated related-work section. It also relocates detailed CIFAR-10 discussion and reorganizes the experimental appendix into modality-specific sections with clearer implementation and evaluation headings.

P2.justification: v2 adds explanatory diagrams, performance curves and image grids in Figures 1–8, plus latency and ImageNet tables. The main CIFAR-10 table becomes a compact summary while the complete original comparison moves to Appendix Table 3. These substantially change how the method and evidence are presented.

improvement.justification: The broader experiments, diversity and latency checks, and implementation details substantially strengthen the empirical paper. However, the relaxed theory introduces a proof defect: in the C.3/D.5 example, q_t(ab)=(1-exp(-2t))/4. Setting epsilon=t and conditioning on ab gives conditional-versus-product TV distance 1/2, while C epsilon²/q_t(ab) tends to zero, contradicting v2's uniform Lemma 1. v1's full-support assumption excludes this unshifted case. The empirical gains coexist with an unsupported theoretical generalization, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
